correctness.rationale: The stationary projector identity and resolvent decomposition are exact. Descartes rule gives one positive simple cubic root, so the scalar stability function has a unique negative minimum; this yields necessary-and-sufficient diagonal positivity with exactly two crossings in the odd subcritical regime. Taylor expansion proves the cusp coefficient. Determinant and an explicit Markov generator prove all embedding assertions. The exact rational example was reconstructed. The actual standalone verifier passed 3360 exact matrix-power/row-sum/positivity checks and deterministic crossing/cusp tests; finite checks are supporting, not the proof.

value.rationale: The two-state chain is the minimal nontrivial conservative kinetic model. This exact rate-imbalance/stepsize/iteration-parity classification establishes when a commonly used L-stable order-two numerical integrator creates a negative transition probability and gives exact recovery under even steps. The square-root cusp resolves a natural sharp boundary, and embedding distinguishes probability-preserving steps from genuine continuous-time transitions. It is a complete natural classification, not an arbitrary parameter slice, trivial sign check or speculative application. Generic equal-input algebra and original scalar stability results are acknowledged as known.
